clue.text: Planted, is plant okay?

parts.note: sat, as in planted or seated oneself firmly
a plant is an industrial works, a factory

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a freshly bedded-in specimen is doing all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted' and 'plant' look horticultural; the second is industrial.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something adequate, good enough to pass.

clue.text: Lengthen sentence

explanation.definitionFit: To stretch is to make longer, and a stretch is a spell in jail.

clue.text: Egyptian king or teacher

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a figure was a pharaoh or a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A private instructor or university supervisor.

clue.text: Demanding second appointment, finally call hospital department

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of appointment

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A patient needs a follow-up booking and at last phones the clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and exacting, imposing rigorous requirements.

clue.text: Writer's wrong conclusion removed

indicators.note: conclusion removed drops the final letter of the wrong word

parts.note: amiss means wrong or awry

explanation.surface: An author's mistaken ending has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' is a link (writer is), not possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and Martin are a father and son of British novelists by this surname.

clue.text: Old and grand wearing tie in concert

indicators.note: wearing means the tie word goes around the other pair of letters like clothing

parts.note: to tether is to tie up
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A distinguished elderly man in a tie attends a musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting jointly or in unison with others.

clue.text: Rent now almost rising somewhere in Yorkshire

parts.note: a rip is a tear or rent

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the letters upwards, from bottom to top
almost drops the last letter of now

explanation.surface: Tenants find housing costs climbing in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cathedral city located in North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Losing king, kept ace in original card game

indicators.note: original means the letters are made into something new, a fresh order
losing signals the king's letter drops out of the pool

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A card player, missing a king but holding an ace, plays an inventive game.
explanation.walkthrough: Take KEPTACEIN, drop the K that 'Losing king' removes, and rearrange the rest ('original').
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire, a game of cards played alone, is called this in Britain.

clue.text: Internet company ignoring last year's awkward delivery

indicators.note: ignoring last drops the final letter of the company name

parts.note: the search giant Google
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A web firm overlooks a recent year's clumsy product launch.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a cricket ball from a leg-spinner that turns the opposite way to the one expected.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a deceptive spin ball awkward for the batsman.

clue.text: Coming back, changing direction again?

definitions.meaning: the question mark flags the punning split

explanation.surface: A traveller heading home keeps switching course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means going back, and read as RE- plus a verb it means making a fresh turn.

clue.text: Asleep, Ian often holds Joanna

indicators.note: the phrase Asleep, Ian often holds the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: Ian, often dozing, embraces a woman named Joanna.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is rhyming slang (Joanna rhymes with a Cockney 'pianner'), so the woman is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang Joanna stands for the keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Large amount of people run in tiny underwear

indicators.note: in places the run's letter within the underwear word

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy undergarment
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A crowd dashes about wearing nothing but skimpy briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd or multitude is a dense mass of people.

clue.text: Staggering, drunk nun isn't good

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving its four letters

explanation.surface: A tipsy nun is shocking behaviour, not good at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishing or astounding, so striking it makes one reel.

clue.text: His Excellency advanced and was first to be cured

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
led, was at the front

explanation.surface: An ambassador moves forward and becomes the first patient to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Made well again, restored to health.

clue.text: Met socialist after a news broadcast

indicators.note: after puts the socialist word behind the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist

explanation.surface: A left-winger shows up following a news bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or challenge is to respond to it satisfactorily.

clue.text: I envy cad's bad, perverted behaviour

indicators.note: bad suggests these letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses jealousy of a scoundrel's wicked, twisted conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct straying from the accepted norm, especially sexually.

clue.text: Approaching naughty child then stopping

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
ending, coming to a halt

explanation.surface: A mischievous child comes near, then halts.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming soon, about to happen, looming.

clue.text: Study Greek island for real

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
Crete, the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone researches a Greek island in earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible and actual, existing in material form rather than abstract.

clue.text: Regularly ruins German fellow's food

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of ruins, starting with the first

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name; with the 's it gives OTTOS

explanation.surface: Every so often a German chap spoils his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian rice dishes are a kind of food.

clue.text: Blow that is with queen's sword

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock or blow
ie, id est, means that is
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A strike delivered with the monarch's blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender, sharp-pointed thrusting blade.

clue.text: Small exercises encapsulating the woman's discipline

indicators.note: encapsulating means the exercises word wraps round the woman word

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise lessons
her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: Short workouts contain a lady's regime of self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity, one's domain of expertise.

clue.text: Fanatical former lover getting married in plane?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in places the married letter inside the plane word

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A zealous ex-partner weds aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical, going to great lengths, far beyond moderate.

clue.text: Bearing gifts for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Someone is carrying presents to give to a crowd of spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bearing or demeanour, an impressive manner, is also called presence.

clue.text: Scoffed each toffee every night? Only at first

indicators.note: only at first takes just the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a toffee is gobbled nightly, then just at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffed means wolfed down or devoured, consumed.

clue.text: Complete discretion after Northern Ireland's backtracking

indicators.note: after puts the discretion word behind the reversed abbreviation
backtracking means the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland
tact is diplomatic discretion

explanation.surface: Total discretion follows a political U-turn in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and undamaged, with nothing missing.

clue.text: American adult caught in trap once more

indicators.note: caught in means the adult letter is held inside the trap word

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
A is the film rating for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up from the US is snared in a trap yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a second time, repeated anew after a previous occasion.

clue.text: Ship's outside northern port

definitions.meaning: the outer body or shell of a vessel
a city and port on the Humber estuary in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the main frame of a vessel and a Yorkshire port city.

clue.text: Horse-riding competition just ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the just word in front of the time letter

parts.note: even means fair or just

explanation.surface: A rider in an equestrian contest finishes barely before the clock runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is a three-part equestrian contest; a single contest is an event.

clue.text: Explain clue I cracked with girlfriend, perhaps

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: a date is a romantic companion, such as a girlfriend; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: A solver boasts of solving a clue together with a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: To make clear or throw light on something is to explain it.

clue.text: Telling niece off for sharpness

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Scolding a niece for being too sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental acuity or cleverness, quickness of mind.
